key_insight: Constitutive Kolmogorov–Arnold networks learn hyperelastic behavior from heterogeneous experiments and yield compact, interpretable closed-form strain energies.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces reliance on expert-selected constitutive formulas and multiple homogeneous tests when calibrating finite element models of soft materials.
method: Embed a constitutive Kolmogorov–Arnold network in finite element model updating.
Train against measured displacement fields and reaction forces.
Use pruning and symbolic regression to obtain closed-form energies satisfying constitutive requirements.
evidence_signal: Natural-rubber tests showed 1–2% median displacement errors and transfer to a withheld hole pattern; additional demonstrations covered single-load silicone calibration and anisotropic aortic inflation.
watch_item: Transfer to a withheld geometry is demonstrated, but extrapolation beyond the measured loading and deformation ranges remains unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Constitutive Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Finite Element Model Updating: Closed-Form Hyperelastic Strain Energies from Heterogeneous Experiments
